useRenderElement(element, componentProps.type: <State, RenderedElementType, TagName, Enabled>(element: TagName, componentProps: {className?, render?, style?}, params?: UseRenderElementParameters) => ReactElement | null
useRenderElement(element, componentProps.semantic: The internal renderer every Base UI part uses. `element` is the default tag; `params.props` accepts a single prop set OR an ARRAY of prop sets / functions (props) => props; returns null when enabled === false.

params.props.semantic: This array-of-prop-sets form is the internal equivalent of mergeProps and is why Base UI parts can layer internal + consumer props without extra allocations.

keyProps.params.state / params.stateAttributesMap: state object and its data-* mapping
keyProps.params.propGetter: @deprecated ((externalProps: HTMLProps) => HTMLProps) — do not use in new code

dataAttributes: Inherits whatever stateAttributesMapping yields (e.g. TransitionStatusDataAttributes: data-starting-style, data-ending-style).
renderProp: Consumes the same `render` prop contract as the public useRender, but couples it to a default tag plus internal prop sets. For author components prefer the public `useRender` ('@base-ui/react/use-render'); useRenderElement is what the library's own parts call.
notableDifferences: No React Aria counterpart — RAC renders through its own internal machinery (useRenderProps/@react-aria/utils) and does not publish an element renderer.

Importing internals couples the repo to unversioned-by-contract APIs (they can change in a minor); a migration should prefer useRender + plain JSX unless it is deliberately re-implementing a Base UI part.
